questions.cardText:
[Zoology] What is the main way sea otters maintain their body heat in cold water?
A. They have a thick layer of blubber like whales
B. They constantly shiver to generate heat
C. Their fur traps a layer of insulating air
Answer: C. Sea otters have the densest fur of any mammal, several hundred times that of human hair. This thick fur coat traps a layer of air next to the otter’s skin, which acts like insulation.
questions.de: Seeotter haben keine Speckschicht – was hält sie stattdessen im kalten Wasser warm?
questions.en: Sea otters have no blubber — what keeps them warm in cold water instead?
questions.answerDe: Ihr dichtes Fell, das eine isolierende Luftschicht festhält
questions.answerEn: Their dense fur, which traps a layer of insulating air

timeline.labelEn: Carl Linnaeus describes the sea otter in the 10th edition of Systema Naturae
timeline.labelDe: Carl von Linné beschreibt den Seeotter in der 10. Auflage der Systema Naturae

questions.notes: Sea otter fur has up to about 130,000–150,000 hairs per cm², the densest of any mammal.

questions.cardText:
[Engineering and Inventions] What was bubble wrap originally designed to be?
A. A toy
B. Wallpaper
C. Insulation
Answer: B. It was originally designed as a type of textured wallpaper in 1957.
questions.de: Als was war Luftpolsterfolie ursprünglich gedacht, als Alfred Fielding und Marc Chavannes sie 1957 erfanden?
questions.en: As what was bubble wrap originally designed when Alfred Fielding and Marc Chavannes invented it in 1957?

timeline.labelEn: Alfred Fielding and Marc Chavannes invent bubble wrap in Hawthorne, New Jersey
timeline.labelDe: Alfred Fielding und Marc Chavannes erfinden in Hawthorne, New Jersey, die Luftpolsterfolie

questions.notes: After failing as wallpaper it was sold as greenhouse insulation, then as packaging (first client IBM, 1961).
